speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What vibrated to manifest the world, and what is the first vibration called?
premises: That Anuttara-formed one, by own desire, willed to manifest all this world.
It vibrated, and that first vibration is called the Śiva-principle by its knowers.
inference: Self-willed vibration of the Highest is the first Śiva-tattva.
uncertainties: Desire-to-manifest object carried into the infinitive.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is Śakti as seed of the world?
premises: Will itself, transparent, ever-co-inherent, being — is power.
She is the seed of the entire moving-and-unmoving world hidden in herself.
inference: Transparent ever-present will-power seeds the self-hidden world.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Who is called Sadāśiva, abiding devoted to all grace?
premises: Having covered the will-emitted world with the Self, abiding.
He indeed, devoted to all grace, is called Sadāśiva.
inference: Self-covering abiding in all-grace is Sadāśiva.
uncertainties: Covering agency, his own act presumed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How does the Lord become all, and what is pure knowledge?
premises: Seeing the universe after himself with this-ness, the Lord has become all.
That becomes pure knowledge, in which this and I are held non-different.
inference: All-become Lordship yields pure knowledge of this-I non-difference.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What does Māyā do to all beings, and what blocks like the shore?
premises: Māyā is difference-notion toward all beings born of own portions.
Always his unbridled power, like the ocean shore, blocks.
inference: Māyā differentiates own-portion beings while unbridled power shore-blocks.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Who is the Person of contracted powers?
premises: He, by her, of limited form with all powers contracted — this is the Person.
Like the dusk-red sun, powers withdrawn, unskilled even in self-shining.
inference: Her contraction makes the limited Person, dusk-sun-like, dim even to himself.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How do his many powers ascend in kalā-form?
premises: Complete doership and the rest — many are his powers.
Through contraction contracted, in kalā-and-rest form, thus they make ascend.
inference: Many powers, contracted into kalā-forms, ascend.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is called kalā?
premises: That all-doership, contracted, directed merely at a few things.
Making him a doer-of-little, it is called kalā by name.
inference: Contracted all-doership directed at few things is kalā.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is declared vidyā by the ancient wise?
premises: His all-knowing power, of limited body, directed merely at little to be known.
Producing knowledge, it is declared vidyā by the ancient wise.
inference: Limited all-knowing power producing knowledge is vidyā.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How has satisfaction become raga-tattva?
premises: Ever-full satisfaction, his very power, yet limited, being.
Ever coloring him toward enjoyments, it has become raga-principle-ness.
inference: Limited ever-satisfaction coloring him toward enjoyments is raga.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How is eternity arranged as the time-principle?
premises: That eternity, his power, having drawn off by giving rise-and-fall.
Making fixed divisions, it is arranged, in time-principle form.
inference: Eternity drawn off through rise-and-fall fixes divisions as time.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How did autonomy-power become restriction?
premises: Which power of his called autonomy, rich in contraction — that very one.
Constraining him helplessly fixed in do-and-do-not, it became restriction.
inference: Autonomy-power contracting into do-don’t constraint is niyati.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is the quiescent collected power of sameness?
premises: The triad-collection of will and the rest — power, quiescent, of contracted form in him.
But consisting in the sameness of sattva and the rest whose nature is collected will and the rest, being.
inference: Collected will-powers rest contracted in guṇa-sameness.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is deemed prakṛti, and what was his will as I-making?
premises: Deemed prakṛti: of the nature of citta whose nature is the fusion of buddhi and the rest.
His will, as rajas-formed I-making effecting I-notion, was.
inference: Fusion-natured citta is prakṛti, and his will was the I-notion-effecting rajas I-making.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What are buddhi and mind?
premises: Even knowledge, of sattva-nature, is the cause of determinative cognition — buddhi.
Its action, dark-formed-bodied, is called mind, the doubting-maker.
inference: Sattvic determinative cause is buddhi, while its dark active body doubting is mind.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How did the contracted-bodied god become manifold objects?
premises: With fivefold division beginning with Vāmā, that very god of contracted body.
Through knowledge-action-tinge predominance became of manifold-object form.
inference: The five-divided contracted god objectifies manifoldly via knowledge-action tinge.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Which are the knowledge-instruments and subtle elements?
premises: Ear, eye, touch, tongue, nose are the knowledge-instruments.
Sound, touch, form, taste, smell — thus the subtle elements.
inference: Five know-organs pair with five subtle elements.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Who is Lord of beings even as elemental self, and what are the five gross?
premises: This very one, most base-born, even as elemental self, is the Lord of beings.
Ether, air, fire, water, earth — the five gross elements.
inference: The base-born elemental self is beings-Lord over the five gross.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What do ear-instruments know, and what are speech and hand?
premises: Beginning with sound, to be known by ear and other instruments — they are the knowns of these.
Speech was the uttering-maker; the hand would be the instrument-being in taking.
inference: Knowns pair with knowers while speech utters and hand takes.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What are foot function and earth-water-fire qualities?
premises: In the triad of going, excreting, bliss — foot and the rest as instrument.
Earth would be smell-possessing; waters naturally fluid; fire.
inference: Foot serves the action-triad while earth-water-fire carry smell-fluidity-heat.
uncertainties: Fire quality carried from the next verse.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What are wind-ether touches, and whom does the poet praise?
premises: Hot touch and formless touch is wind; ether with sound.
I praise the Kaula consisting of thirty-six principles, beyond the kula — Śambhu.
inference: Wind-ether complete the elements, and the poet praises the thirty-six-principled beyond-kula Śambhu.
